selection_rule: Top three unique retrieved records in search rank order; fixed before generation. No model-based selection or quality-driven replacement.
hypothesis: With the task request and learner repertoire fixed, available mathematical reference evidence may improve mathematical validity and preservation of the intended target without disclosing the central idea. B minus A is grounding availability; C minus B is incremental Learning Commons availability. No change or worse validity/openness is a null or negative result, not a reason to tune or replace outputs.
limitations: New PF task-family specifications, not proven untouched topics. Related MCQ topics and adjacent PF sweep topics have previously been inspected; every main case is conservatively labelled transfer.
This tests evidence availability during design, not independent prerequisite discovery: D1 is a fixed stipulated learner record in every arm.
Curriculum pages describe an entire secondary course and can contain later mathematics. References are explicitly not evidence that this learner knows those topics.
Learning Commons standards are additional mathematical references, not a Singapore curriculum replacement or learner prior knowledge.
Reference text lengths differ across arms and are part of the treatment; this is not an equal-token-content experiment.
Generation alone is not evidence of approach diversity, student behaviour, productive failure, or learning.

shared_context.subject: mathematics
shared_context.task_rule: Generate a new student task for exploration before instruction on the target. Preserve the requested task family without requiring unrelated additional prerequisites. Do not give a worked example or a lesson.
shared_context.provenance_rule: Use fictional task data where needed. Do not claim invented records are observations.

learner_context.profile_status: Hypothetical stipulated learner specification, not observed students.
learner_context.prior_boundary: Only the case-specific recently taught resources in the fixed D1 packet are assumed. The target method has not been taught; retrieved descriptions do not expand this repertoire.

cases.topic: scientific notation and comparing very large and small quantities
cases.target_concept: Representing and comparing quantities using a coefficient and a power of ten, including choosing a consistent scale. Learners have not been taught normalized scientific notation.
cases.task_family: Design a compact, unambiguous comparison record for measurements with very different magnitudes. Students choose and justify a common recording and comparison convention rather than merely convert a supplied list to a prescribed format.
teacher_recently_taught: Decimal place value and comparison
Multiplication and division of decimals by powers of ten
Positive integer powers as repeated multiplication
Reading numerical measurement tables
cases.history_note: No identical PF expert-comparison or twenty-topic sweep case. Decimal and unit-conversion MCQ work is adjacent; no claim that the topic is untouched.
cases.local_query: scientific notation standard form powers of ten
cases.lc_query: scientific notation powers of ten comparing large and small numbers

cases.target_concept: A coherent rule for multiplying signed integers, including two negative factors, derived from familiar addition and subtraction rather than a supplied sign rule.
cases.task_family: Create and defend a consistent way of recording repeated additions and removals of gains and debts in a fictional ledger. Students must compare possible recording conventions across cases; no unrelated finance formula is needed.
teacher_recently_taught: Signed numbers on a number line
Addition and subtraction of signed integers
Multiplication of nonnegative whole numbers as equal groups
Reading a table of changes and balances
cases.history_note: Negative numbers occur in the MCQ pathway benchmark, but this ledger PF specification is not an expert-comparison or twenty-topic sweep case.
cases.lc_query: multiply positive and negative integers rational numbers sign rules

cases.topic: distributive property and equivalent algebraic expressions
cases.target_concept: Recognizing and justifying equivalence of a grouped product and an expanded sum for a variable quantity. Learners have not been taught the algebraic distributive rule.
cases.task_family: Compare competing general price-recording rules for bundles containing fixed and variable items, and develop a defensible rule valid across bundle sizes. Numerical testing is accessible but students must decide what makes the comparison convincing.
teacher_recently_taught: Arithmetic with parentheses and order of operations
Whole-number multiplication and addition
Substituting values into simple expressions
Letters representing a variable quantity
cases.history_note: Algebraic distribution occurs in the MCQ pathway benchmark. This bundle-rule task family is new to the PF expert comparison and sweep.
cases.lc_query: distributive property equivalent expressions expand factor linear expressions

cases.topic: conversion between square centimetres and square metres
cases.target_concept: Area-unit conversion depends on two dimensions, rather than copying the length conversion factor. Learners have not been taught a square-unit conversion rule.
cases.task_family: Choose between fictional material offers expressed using different area units and package sizes, and design a fair comparison record for a rectangular project. Students decide how to represent the units and usable quantities; no surface-area optimization or percentage discount is required.
teacher_recently_taught: Rectangle area from side lengths
Converting centimetres and metres for lengths
Multiplication and division of decimals
Comparing simple unit prices
cases.history_note: Adjacent to the previous length/area-scaling PF sweep and unit-conversion MCQ cases, but the mixed-unit offer task is a different specification.

cases.lc_query: convert square units area square centimeters square meters measurement

cases.topic: interior angle sums of convex polygons
cases.target_concept: Relating the number of sides of a convex polygon to its interior angle sum and using this to reason about regular corners. Learners have not been taught a polygon-angle-sum formula.
cases.task_family: Develop a defensible corner-checking record for proposed regular polygon tiles meeting at a point. Students choose representations and checks for possible tile combinations using angle facts they already know; no trigonometry or formal tessellation theorem is needed.
teacher_recently_taught: Angles around a point sum to a full turn
Triangle interior angles sum to 180 degrees
Drawing and measuring angles

cases.history_note: Triangle angles occur in the MCQ pathway benchmark. No identical polygon-angle PF case in the prior expert comparison or twenty-topic sweep.
